reduced_findings.location: Section 8 — Upstream ADR tag line; recovery behavior asserted in Section 5 (degraded→recovered, RTO ≤ 30 min) and Section 7 (degraded-mode and recovery contract)
reduced_findings.message: The SPEC asserts RTO-bounded recovery (Section 5 state transition 'from degraded to recovered — resolves resume within RTO ≤ 30 min'; Section 7 contract 'Store degradation returns a bounded error, then recovers within RTO'), which traces to ADR-01 consequence ADR.01.05.cb92 (mature recovery tooling — PITR + standby promotion meeting RTO ≤ 30 min, BDD.01.03.44fe). That ADR element is the named upstream commitment for the recovery claim, but it is not carried in the Section 8 Upstream ADR tag line, whereas the sibling consequences (.47a1, .454a, .5896, .7dde, .2740) are. The section-level trace for the recovery behavior is therefore thinner than for the other inherited commitments. No contradiction — the behavior is consistent with ADR-01; only the explicit upstream linkage is absent.
reduced_findings.recommendation: Add @adr: ADR.01.05.cb92 to the Section 8 Upstream ADR list so the RTO-recovery behavior in Section 5 and the recovery contract in Section 7 trace explicitly to the ADR consequence that committed PITR + standby promotion for RTO ≤ 30 min.

reduced_findings.location: Section 3 — increment_visit delivery contract / Section 6 — dead-letter recovery
reduced_findings.message: Dead-letter recovery closes the exactly-once loop via 'operator action' replay through the idempotent increment path, but the recovery time of that reconciliation tail is unbounded. The count-staleness window bounds WHEN an event is routed to dead-letter (and alerted), not WHEN a dead-lettered or out-of-window-skew event is reconciled — that step waits on an operator with no MTTR/RTO. RTO ≤ 30 min is scoped to store-loss recovery, not the dead-letter replay tail. A backlog of dead-lettered count events can therefore stay unreconciled indefinitely while still meeting every stated bound.
reduced_findings.recommendation: State a recovery-time bound (or explicit SLO/escalation target) for dead-letter reconciliation — e.g. dead-lettered events must be replayed within a named operator-response window, with the dead-letter counter feeding an SLA-bounded alert. Make the manual-reconciliation MTTR testable at TDD-01 alongside the RTO ≤ 30 min store-loss probe.

reduced_findings.location: Section 3 — Delivery channel (Visit-Counter-owned durable queue) / Section 6 — Read/create design-load
reduced_findings.message: The durable async dispatch queue that carries increment_visit off the redirect path has no characterized beyond-margin behavior: when the reconciler sustainably lags the producer, queue depth grows on durable storage with no stated bound or shed/backpressure policy. The off-path design correctly protects redirects, and the queue is owned by the Visit Counter — but SPEC-01 binds the at-least-once contract to that transport, so its saturation policy is in-scope to reference. Unbounded durable-queue growth under sustained count load is the un-addressed tail.
reduced_findings.recommendation: Reference the queue's beyond-margin policy: bound the durable backlog (max depth / age) and state what happens at that bound (shed-with-alert vs. block producer vs. age-out to dead-letter), tying it to the existing reconciliation-lag metric. If the policy lives entirely in the Visit Counter component spec, cite that owner explicitly so the backpressure contract is traceable rather than absent.

reduced_findings.message: The ShortCode charset/length allowlist precondition names only resolve and mark_taken_down. read_original_url also accepts an attacker-influenceable ShortCode but is not listed under the defense-in-depth re-validation rule, so it is the one classified-read interface whose code argument is guarded solely by the parameterized PK lookup. By the SPEC's own stated defense-in-depth parity principle, the classified PII read deserves at least the same store-boundary code validation as the unprivileged resolve.
reduced_findings.recommendation: Extend the Section 5 ShortCode allowlist validation rule to include read_original_url (i.e., 'resolve, read_original_url, and mark_taken_down accept only a ShortCode matching the code-generation charset/length allowlist'), giving the highest-sensitivity read the same boundary precondition as the others.

reduced_findings.message: increment_visit accepts an EventId (event_id) that serves as the dedup/idempotency key, but no input-validation rule constrains its format/length. The dedup key is attacker-influenceable on the visit edge; an unbounded or malformed EventId could be used to bloat the dedup index or craft collisions against the idempotency gate. Risk is bounded because the consumer is idempotent and off the synchronous path, but no typed-parse/length rule is specified at the store boundary for this security-relevant key.
reduced_findings.recommendation: Add a Section 5 validation rule that increment_visit accepts only a typed/parsed EventId of bounded length/format (typed-parse or schema-validate) as a store-boundary precondition, paralleling the put_mapping OriginalUrl and resolve ShortCode allowlist rules.
